verses.1: Saul was in agreement with his killing. On that day a great persecution began against the assembly in Jerusalem; all the members scattered into the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.
verses.2: Devout men carried Stephen out and made a great burial for him.
verses.3: Saul was troubling the assembly house by house, dragging both men and women down to prison.
verses.4: The ones scattered went about proclaiming the message.
verses.5: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Messiah there.
verses.6: The crowds listened with one accord to what Philip was saying and watched the signs he performed.
verses.7: Many who had unclean spirits cried out in loud voices as they came out, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
verses.8: A great joy filled that city.
verses.9: A man named Simon had previously been prominent in the city, doing magic and amazing the Samaritan people, claiming to be someone great.
verses.10: Everyone paid attention to him, from the smallest to the greatest, saying, "This man is the Great Power of God called the Great."
verses.11: They were drawn to him because for a long time his magic had stunned them.
verses.12: When they believed what Philip was proclaiming, regarding the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus the Messiah, they were baptized, both men and women.
verses.13: Simon also believed, and having been baptized, he clung to Philip, astonished at the great signs and wonders that were being done.
verses.14: When those in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
verses.15: These men went down and prayed for them so that they might receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.16: For the Holy Spirit had not yet come upon any of them, only they had been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.17: Then the apostles laid hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
verses.18: But when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he brought them money
verses.19: and said, "Give me this power too, so that anyone to whom I lay hands may receive the Holy Spirit."
verses.20: Peter said to him, "May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money.
verses.21: You have no share or part in this word, for your heart is not upright before God.
verses.22: Therefore, repent of this wickedness of yours and pray to the Lord, in case perhaps the thought in your heart may be forgiven you.
verses.23: For I see that you are in bitter anger and bound in a knot of iniquity."
verses.24: Simon replied, "Pray for me to the Lord so that nothing of what you have said may come upon me."
verses.25: So, after testifying and speaking the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, proclaiming the gospel in many Samaritan villages.
verses.26: An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Get up and go south along the road that descends from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is a wilderness."
verses.27: Rising up, he went, and behold, an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of her entire treasury, who had come to Jerusalem to worship,
verses.28: was returning and seated in his chariot, reading the prophet Isaiah.
verses.29: The Spirit said to Philip, "Go up and join that chariot."
verses.30: Running up, Philip heard him reading Isaiah the prophet and said, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
verses.31: He replied, "How can I unless someone guides me?" And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
verses.32: The section of the scripture he was reading was this: "Like a lamb led to the slaughter, and like a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he opened not his mouth.
verses.33: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away; who will declare his generation? For his life is taken from the earth."
verses.34: The eunuch answered Philip, "I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this—about himself or about someone else?"
verses.35: Philip opened his mouth and began from that scripture to proclaim Jesus to him.
verses.36: As they were going along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, "Look, water. What hinders me from being baptized?"
verses.37: Philip said, "If you believe with all your heart, you may." And he answered, "I believe that Jesus is the Son of God."
verses.38: Then he ordered the chariot to stop, and both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
verses.39: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught up Philip, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
verses.40: Philip was found in Azotus, and he traveled through all the cities, proclaiming the good news until he came to Caesarea.

notes:
Notes
- v. 37: The verse number was missing in the initial translation; the source text includes verse 37, which explains the eunuch's belief and Philip's response.
